Mount Shasta.title: Mount Shasta
Mount Shasta.what: Mount Shasta is a potentially active stratovolcano at the southern end of the Cascade Range in Siskiyou County, California.
Mount Shasta.history: At an elevation of 14,179 ft (4,322 m), it is the second-highest peak in the Cascades and the fifth-highest in the state. Mount Shasta has an estimated volume of 85 cubic miles, which makes it the most voluminous stratovolcano in the Cascade Volcanic Arc.

Mount McLoughlin.title: Mount McLoughlin
Mount McLoughlin.what: Mount McLoughlin is a 9,493 ft (2,893 m) dormant steep-sided stratovolcano, or composite volcano, in the Cascade Range of southern Oregon, United States.
Mount McLoughlin.history: Oregon's legislature renamed it from Mount Pitt in 1905, for Dr. John McLoughlin, a central figure in early Oregon history.

Pelican Butte.title: Pelican Butte
Pelican Butte.what: Pelican Butte is a steep-sided shield volcano in the Cascade Range of southern Oregon, United States.
Pelican Butte.history: It is located 28 mi (45 km) due south of Crater Lake and 12 mi (19 km) northeast of Mount McLoughlin. Pelican Butte is the most prominent shield volcano in the southern Oregon Cascades and has a large volume at 4.8 cu mi (20 km3), making it one of the bigger Quaternary volcanoes in the region, approaching the size of some of the range's stratovolcanoes.

Mount Scott.title: Mount Scott
Mount Scott.what: The highest point of Crater Lake National Park, 8,929 feet, on the east side of the caldera.
Mount Scott.history: It is the oldest peak of Mount Mazama, built about 420,000 years ago; Mazama's collapse 7,700 years ago made the caldera that holds Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States.

Mount Thielsen.title: Mount Thielsen
Mount Thielsen.what: Mount Thielsen, is an extinct shield volcano in the Oregon High Cascades, near Mount Bailey.
Mount Thielsen.history: Because eruptive activity ceased 250,000 years ago, glaciers have heavily eroded the volcano's structure, creating precipitous slopes and a horn-like peak. The spire-like shape of Thielsen attracts lightning strikes and creates fulgurite, an unusual mineral.

Diamond Peak.title: Diamond Peak
Diamond Peak.what: An 8,744-foot volcano on the Cascade crest above Willamette Pass, the highest summit in this part of the range.
Diamond Peak.history: Great glaciers carved it after the volcanic activity that built it; about 14 miles of the Pacific Crest Trail cross its wilderness.

Maiden Peak.title: Maiden Peak
Maiden Peak.what: Maiden Peak is a steep-sided shield volcano in the Cascade Range of central Oregon.
Maiden Peak.history: It is the highest point in the 43-mile (69 km) distance between Mount Bachelor and Diamond Peak. Ice Age glaciers carved a large cirque into the northeast flank of the mountain, exposing magma which hardened in the volcano's conduits to form the numerous rock pinnacles now found in the upper part of the cirque.

Mount Bachelor.title: Mount Bachelor
Mount Bachelor.what: Mount Bachelor, formerly named Bachelor Butte, is a dormant stratovolcano atop a shield volcano in the Cascade Volcanic Arc and the Cascade Range of central Oregon, United States.
Mount Bachelor.history: Named Mount Bachelor because it stands apart from the nearby Three Sisters, it lies in the eastern segment of the central portion of the High Cascades, the eastern segment of the Cascade Range. The volcano lies at the northern end of the 15-mile (24 km) long Mount Bachelor Volcanic Chain, which underwent four major eruptive episodes during the Pleistocene and the Holocene.

Lake Ewauna and the Klamath River.title: Lake Ewauna
Lake Ewauna and the Klamath River.what: The broad first two miles of the Klamath River at Klamath Falls, fed by the Link River from Upper Klamath Lake.
Lake Ewauna and the Klamath River.history: George Nurse founded Linkville, now Klamath Falls, in 1867 where the Link River meets Lake Ewauna; William S. Moore and his son built its first sawmill on the Link River in 1877, and the town took its present name in 1893.

Upper Klamath Lake.title: Upper Klamath Lake
Upper Klamath Lake.what: Oregon's largest body of fresh water by surface area, large and shallow, about 25 miles long and 8 wide, northwest of Klamath Falls.
Upper Klamath Lake.history: The Treaty of 1864 merged the Klamath, Modoc and Yahooskin into one tribe on a reservation in the basin; in 1954 Congress ended its federal recognition, restored in 1986. Calvin Coolidge set apart the Upper Klamath refuge on April 3, 1928.

links.label: Water shortages test tribes, farmers and wildlife

Odell Lake.title: Odell Lake
Odell Lake.what: A glacier-carved lake at Willamette Pass in the Deschutes National Forest; the railroad runs along its southwest shore.
Odell Lake.history: Bynon J. Pengra named it in July 1865 for Oregon Surveyor General William Holman Odell, while surveying the military road that became Oregon Route 58; a glacier's terminal moraine holds the water in along its southeast shore.
